spitsbergen.name: Spitsbergen
spitsbergen.summary: The largest island of Norway's Svalbard archipelago in the Arctic, used as a whaling base in the 17th and 18th centuries and later for coal mining.

smeerenburg.name: Smeerenburg
smeerenburg.summary: A Dutch and Danish whaling station founded in 1619 on Amsterdam Island in Svalbard, abandoned around 1660 once local whales were hunted out.

davis-strait.name: Davis Strait
davis-strait.summary: An arm of the Arctic Ocean between Greenland and Baffin Island, named for explorer John Davis and used for whale hunting from the 1650s.

baffin-island.name: Baffin Island
baffin-island.summary: The largest island in Canada and second-largest in the Americas, in Nunavut at 68°N; inhabited for at least 3,000 years, it now has about 13,000 residents.

south-sea-company.name: South Sea Company
south-sea-company.summary: A British company founded in 1711 to manage government debt, later granted a monopoly on selling enslaved Africans; its collapsing stock caused the 1720 South Sea Bubble.

willem-barentsz.name: Willem Barentsz
willem-barentsz.summary: Dutch navigator and Arctic explorer (c. 1550–1597) who searched for a Northeast Passage; his voyages led to the discovery of Spitsbergen, and the Barents Sea bears his name.

little-ice-age.name: Little Ice Age
little-ice-age.summary: A period of regional cooling, mainly in the North Atlantic, usually dated from the 16th to 19th centuries or as early as 1300, with proposed causes including solar and volcanic activity.

thule-people.name: Thule people
thule-people.summary: The precursors of modern Inuit and Yupik peoples, who developed in coastal Alaska by 1000 CE, spread across the Arctic, and replaced the earlier Dorset culture by the 15th century.

umiak.name: Umiak
umiak.summary: Open skin boat used by the Yupik and Inuit across Arctic coastal areas, traditionally used in summer to move people and to hunt whales and walrus.

bj-rn-ya.name: Bjørnøya
bj-rn-ya.summary: The southernmost island of Norway's Svalbard archipelago, discovered by Dutch explorers in 1596 and named for a polar bear seen swimming nearby.

svalbard.name: Svalbard
svalbard.summary: A Norwegian Arctic archipelago between mainland Norway and the North Pole, used by whalers from the 17th-18th centuries and later developed for coal mining; recognized as Norwegian territory in 1920.

f-hr.name: Föhr
f-hr.summary: A North Frisian island off Germany's North Sea coast, formed in 1362 when a storm flood split the mainland coastline; it belonged to Denmark until 1864, when it passed to Prussia.

copper-inuit.name: Copper Inuit
copper-inuit.summary: A Canadian Inuit group, also called Inuinnait, who historically lived around Coronation Gulf and Victoria Island and relied on native copper from the Coppermine River.

netsilik.name: Netsilik
netsilik.summary: An Inuit people living mainly around Kugaaruk and Gjoa Haven in Nunavut, Canada, among the last northern Indigenous peoples to encounter missionaries in the early 20th century.

sisimiut.name: Sisimiut
sisimiut.summary: The second-largest city in Greenland, settled for about 4,500 years by the Saqqaq, Dorset and Thule peoples before Danish settlement in the 1720s.

sisimiut-museum.name: Poul Madsen collection
sisimiut-museum.summary: A collection of handcraft, art, house items and ethnographic objects compiled over fifty years, held at the Sisimiut Museum in Greenland.

hans-egede.name: Hans Egede
hans-egede.summary: Norwegian Lutheran missionary priest (1686–1758) called the 'Apostle of Greenland' for reviving Danish-Norwegian contact with the island after about 300 years, and founder of its capital, Nuuk.

garrett-hardin.name: Garrett Hardin
garrett-hardin.summary: An American ecologist (1915-2003) best known for the concept of the 'tragedy of the commons,' though also noted for racist and anti-immigrant views.

tragedy-of-the-commons.name: Tragedy of the commons
tragedy-of-the-commons.summary: The idea that individuals sharing a resource are driven to overuse it even though this depletes it for everyone; the term comes from a 1968 essay by ecologist Garrett Hardin.

bergen-greenland-company.name: Bergen Greenland Company
bergen-greenland-company.summary: A Dano-Norwegian corporation that founded and ran Danish-Norwegian colonies and trade in Greenland from 1721 until going bankrupt in 1727.

nipisat-island.name: Nipisat Island
nipisat-island.summary: A small, uninhabited island in the Qeqqata municipality of central-western Greenland.

jacob-severin.name: Jacob Severin
jacob-severin.summary: Danish merchant who held a trade monopoly on Greenland from 1733 to 1749.

thule.name: Thule
thule.summary: A legendary, extremely remote northern land described by ancient Greek and Roman writers, later variously identified with places like Iceland, Greenland or Scandinavia.

joik.name: Joik
joik.summary: Traditional Sámi song form from Northern Europe, in which each performance is meant to reflect or evoke a specific person, animal or place.

johannes-schefferus.name: Johannes Schefferus
johannes-schefferus.summary: Swedish humanist (1621–1679), one of the most important of his time, also known as Angelus and remembered for writing hymns.

lapponia-book.name: Lapponia
lapponia-book.summary: A 1673 Latin book by Johannes Schefferus describing the geography and Sámi way of life of Northern Scandinavia, translated into English in 1674 as The History of Lapland.

gar-ar-greenland.name: Garðar
gar-ar-greenland.summary: The seat of the bishop in Norse Greenland, and the first Catholic diocese established anywhere in the Americas.

greenlandic-norse.name: Greenlandic Norse
greenlandic-norse.summary: An extinct North Germanic language spoken in Norse Greenland until the settlements' demise in the late 15th century, known mainly from runic inscriptions and believed to have been in contact with the Greenlandic language.

ambrose-philips.name: Ambrose Philips
ambrose-philips.summary: English poet and politician (1674–1749) whose feuds with rivals earned him the mocking nickname "Namby-Pamby."

adolphus-greely.name: Adolphus Greely
adolphus-greely.summary: American Army officer and polar explorer (1844–1935) who led a disastrous 1881 Arctic expedition and later became the Army's Chief Signal Officer.

manuel-i-of-portugal.name: Manuel I of Portugal
manuel-i-of-portugal.summary: King of Portugal from 1495 to 1521, known as the Fortunate, whose reign saw major overseas expansion including Vasco da Gama's sea route to India and Cabral's discovery of Brazil.

gaspar-corte-real.name: Gaspar Corte-Real
gaspar-corte-real.summary: Portuguese explorer (1450, disappeared 1501) who took part in voyages sponsored by the Portuguese Crown said to be among the first to reach Newfoundland and eastern Canada.

ercole-i-d-este.name: Ercole I d'Este
ercole-i-d-este.summary: Duke of Ferrara, Modena, and Reggio from 1471 until his death in 1505, known for patronizing the arts and strengthening his duchy's economy and political standing.

cantino-planisphere.name: Cantino planisphere
cantino-planisphere.summary: A Portuguese world map from 1502, smuggled from Portugal to Italy, notable as the earliest surviving map to show Portuguese discoveries including the Brazilian coast and southern Greenland.

johannes-ruysch.name: Johannes Ruysch
johannes-ruysch.summary: Dutch cartographer, explorer, painter and Benedictine monk from Utrecht (c. 1470–1533), best known for one of the earliest printed maps to show parts of the New World, in his 1508 world map.

gerardus-mercator.name: Gerardus Mercator
gerardus-mercator.summary: Flemish geographer and cartographer (1512-1594) famed for his 1569 world map projection, still used in nautical charts, and for producing the first work called an 'atlas'.

martin-waldseem-ller.name: Martin Waldseemüller
martin-waldseem-ller.summary: German cartographer (c. 1470–1520) who, with Matthias Ringmann, first used the name "America" on a 1507 world map, the first to show the Americas as a landmass separate from Asia.

john-davis-explorer.name: John Davis
john-davis-explorer.summary: English explorer and navigator (c. 1550–1605) who searched for the Northwest Passage and discovered the Falkland Islands in August 1592.

disko-bay.name: Disko Bay
disko-bay.summary: Large bay on Greenland's western coast, forming an inlet of Baffin Bay.

christian-iv-of-denmark.name: Christian IV of Denmark
christian-iv-of-denmark.summary: King of Denmark and Norway from 1588 to 1648, Scandinavia's longest-reigning monarch, remembered for ambitious reforms and for leading Denmark–Norway into the costly Thirty Years' War.

james-hall-explorer.name: James Hall
james-hall-explorer.summary: An English explorer (d. 1612) who piloted three Danish expeditions to Greenland, charting its west coast, and died there after a violent encounter with Inuit.

cape-farewell-greenland.name: Cape Farewell
cape-farewell-greenland.summary: The southernmost point of Greenland, a headland on Egger Island regarded as one of the country's important landmarks.

carl-linnaeus.name: Carl Linnaeus
carl-linnaeus.summary: Swedish biologist and physician (1707–1778) who formalized binomial nomenclature, the modern system of naming organisms, and is known as the father of modern taxonomy.

systema-naturae.name: Systema Naturae
systema-naturae.summary: A major work by Swedish naturalist Carl Linnaeus, first published in 1735, that introduced the Linnaean system of naming and classifying living things.

frobisher-bay.name: Frobisher Bay
frobisher-bay.summary: A 230 km inlet off Baffin Island in Nunavut, Canada, long assumed to be a strait until it was confirmed to be a bay in 1861.

martin-frobisher.name: Martin Frobisher
martin-frobisher.summary: English sea captain and privateer (c. 1535–1594) who made three voyages seeking the Northwest Passage and was later knighted for helping repel the Spanish Armada in 1588.

frederick-ii-of-denmark.name: Frederick II of Denmark
frederick-ii-of-denmark.summary: King of Denmark and Norway from 1559 to 1588, whose reign brought peace and prosperity after his father's civil war, with building projects at Kronborg and Frederiksborg; father of Christian IV.

james-alday.name: James Alday
james-alday.summary: A 16th-century English navigator, explorer and privateer credited, along with Sebastian Cabot and Henry Ostrich, with starting regular trade between England and the Barbary coast.

denmark-norway.name: Denmark-Norway
denmark-norway.summary: A real union of the kingdoms of Denmark and Norway (with Norway's overseas possessions) plus Schleswig and Holstein, lasting from the 16th to 19th centuries.

treaty-of-tordesillas.name: Treaty of Tordesillas
treaty-of-tordesillas.summary: 1494 treaty dividing newly discovered lands outside Europe between Portugal and Castile along a meridian west of Cape Verde.

miguel-corte-real.name: Miguel Corte-Real
miguel-corte-real.summary: A Portuguese explorer (c. 1448–1502?) who charted about 600 miles of the coast of Labrador before disappearing at sea in 1502.

treaty-of-kiel.name: Treaty of Kiel
treaty-of-kiel.summary: A January 1814 treaty in which Denmark's Frederick VI ceded Heligoland to Britain and Norway to Sweden in exchange for Swedish Pomerania, while keeping Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands.

moravian-church.name: Moravian Church
moravian-church.summary: The German name for the Moravian Church, a Protestant denomination with roots in the 15th-century Bohemian Reformation, known for its worldwide missionary work.

nuuk.name: Nuuk
nuuk.summary: Capital and largest city of Greenland, founded in 1728 by Danish-Norwegian missionary Hans Egede as Godthaab; renamed Nuuk after home rule began in 1979.

angakkuq.name: Angakkuq
angakkuq.summary: A spiritual and intellectual figure in Inuit culture who serves a role similar to a medicine man or shaman, with comparable figures found among other Alaska Native peoples.

paul-egede.name: Paul Egede
paul-egede.summary: Dano-Norwegian theologian and missionary (1708–1789) who continued the Lutheran mission among the Kalaallit people in Greenland begun by his father, Hans Egede.

inughuit.name: Inughuit
inughuit.summary: An ethnic subgroup of Greenlandic Inuit, the northernmost group of Inuit and people in North America, making up about 1% of Greenland's population.

akunnat.name: Lichtenfels (Akunnat)
akunnat.summary: A former Moravian mission settlement, called Lichtenfels, in southern Greenland, founded in 1748 by missionaries and Inuit families and later handed to the Lutheran Church of Denmark in 1900.

alluitsoq.name: Lichtenau (Alluitsoq)
alluitsoq.summary: Moravian mission settlement founded in southern Greenland in 1774, once the largest permanent settlement in Greenland, before its mission passed to the Danish Lutheran Church in 1900.

kalaallit.name: Kalaallit
kalaallit.summary: The largest indigenous group in Greenland, part of the Inuit people, whose language, Kalaallisut, is known in English as Greenlandic.

tupilaq.name: Tupilaq
tupilaq.summary: A monster figure in Inuit religion, especially in Greenland, traditionally fashioned by a shaman from animal and human remains to attack an enemy; today carved as a popular art form.

igloolik.name: Iglulingmiut
igloolik.summary: The Inuktitut name for the people of Igloolik, a hamlet in Nunavut, Canada; it means 'people of the house,' referring to old sod dwellings rather than snow igloos.
